jobs.description:
**Company Description**  

* **Application Opening:** October 7, 2026
* **Application Deadline:** May close at any time but not before October 21, 2026
* **Work Location:** Hybrid with onsite and remote weekly schedule
* **Shift:** Monday-Friday: 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM (Full-Time)
* **Salary:** $134,082.00 - $168,688.00

**Appointment Type**

This is a Temporary Exempt (TEX), full-time position. This position is excluded by the Charter from the competitive Civil Service examination process, is considered “at will” and shall serve at the discretion of the Appointing Officer. The duration of the appointment shall not exceed 36 months.

**Who We Are**

Through the provision of coordinated, compassionate, and high‐quality services, the Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing strives to make homelessness in San Francisco rare, brief, and one time. The Department provides assistance and support to homeless and at‐risk youth, adults and families to prevent imminent episodes of homelessness and end homelessness for people in San Francisco. Services including outreach, homelessness prevention, emergency shelter, drop‐in centers, transitional housing, supportive housing, short‐term rental subsidies, and support services to help people exit homelessness. For more information on the department, please visit our https://hsh.sfgov.org/.

**What We Do**

San Francisco is a pioneer in homeless services and a leader in providing supportive housing as a permanent exit from homelessness. The Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH), founded in 2016, is a national leader in the movement to end homelessness by developing a coordinated, equity-driven, client-focused system of compassionate services while piloting innovative models, and implementing best practice solutions with measurable results.

HSH’s Homelessness Response System (HRS) oversees and implements a system of care that shelters, houses, and serves approximately 15,000 people daily. Major programs include: street outreach and service connection through the Homeless Outreach Team (SFHOT); 3,600 + bed shelter system for transitional age youth, adults and families including shelters for members of the LGBTQ community; rapid rehousing rental subsidies for families, adults, older adults, and transitional aged youth; the Problem Solving and flexible financial assistance programs; and robust supportive housing programs with over 14, 500 units which provide housing and services to formerly homeless transitional age youth, individuals, and families.

 **Job Description**

The Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH) has an exciting opportunity for an excellent communicator, experienced business analyst, and energetic individual who is passionate about solving homelessness for our community. This highly motivated and team-oriented person will play a key role within the Department’s ONE System Team. Under the general direction of the ONE System Director, the Senior IS Business Analyst will oversee and provide technical leadership for ONE System processes and projects.

The ONE System is an enterprise Software as a Service (SaaS) system and serves as San Francisco’s Homeless Management Information System (HMIS). The ONE System supports HSH and its 75+ community-based organizations to provide a unified system for the City’s Homelessness Response System. The ONE System operationalizes, streamlines, and tracks workflows related to outreach, assessment, prioritization, referral, and placement for families, youth, and individuals seeking housing, shelter and other vital programs and services.

The Senior Business Analyst will support and oversee key aspects of a project to automate the flow of case management data via APIs from individual provider/CBO systems into the ONE System. Currently, providers spend significant time entering duplicative information into their own case management system and the ONE System. By replacing duplicative, manual tasks with an automated data flow, provider case managers can devote more time serving clients. The position will work with various project stakeholders, including HSH program teams, the Department of Technology, community providers, and the ONE System software vendor. The position will generate technical documentation, participate in testing and quality assurance activities, build and maintain dashboards to monitor data and track key metrics, help troubleshoot technical issues, and make process improvement recommendations.

The successful candidate will be a good listener with the ability to work collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders and the software vendor. They will bridge communication gaps between these groups to meaningfully contribute to the success of the project. If you love finding ways to use technology to help improve the lives of people, this might be the perfect opportunity for you.

**Essential duties include, but are not limited to:**

* Develop technical documentation (e.g., data dictionaries and mapping templates) to support ingesting data from external systems into ONE via an API.
* Analyze ONE System API security permissions to determine required appropriate configuration for secure, connected API integration without granting more access than is needed.
* Support stakeholder communication and engagement by developing slide decks and targeted messaging materials for information sessions. Help facilitate and/or present at stakeholder meetings.
* Contribute to a “Provider API Onboarding Toolkit”, which will serve as a scalable toolkit to streamline the onboarding process for providers to participate in the project.
* Provide data mapping guidance to providers on mapping their source data structures into the required format for successful ingestion into ONE.
* Oversee aspects of testing to validate workflows and system stability for each provider as part of the onboarding process. Support live-data pilot within a secure test environment prior to productio

Muon Space seeks a Senior Program Manager to lead delivery of next-generation satellites for national security missions, including missile warning and tracking. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role at the intersection of payload engineering and rapid-cycle space vehicle development.

The Senior PM is the accountable owner for delivering the program on cost, schedule, and technical performance. You will manage a multi-disciplinary internal team, subcontractors, and a critical-path vendor base for EO/IR payloads, algorithm development, avionics, and space vehicle builds. This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

--------------------

jobs.title: Logistics Procurement Program Manager
jobs.description:
**What to Expect**

Tesla is focused on building a world of abundance and we are seeking a Logistics Procurement Program Manager to manage execution of logistics procurement programs. You will coordinate between the operations stakeholders requesting logistics services and logistics supply chain managers responsible for sourcing those services. You will ensure that requirements, statements of work, and service-level agreements are defined, aligned, and progressing, and that major programs, including capital expenditure programs, advance from request through start of service on an agreed timeline. You will manage multiple logistics projects concurrently, across the modes each program requires. Category strategy and commercial negotiation remain with the supply managers. This is a high-ownership role for someone who can keep a portfolio of programs on schedule and present status, risks, and decisions to a broad group of stakeholders.

  
**What You'll Do**

* **Program Portfolio Ownership & Governance:** Own a cross-category portfolio of logistics programs by establishing scope, timelines, accountable owners, and success criteria for each; maintain a program operating cadence including milestone reviews, a risk log, and status reporting suitable for leadership; and ensure a repeatable coordination process that does not depend on a single individual
* **Stakeholder Coordination & Escalation:** Serve as the coordination point between operations stakeholders requesting logistics services and supply chain managers procuring them, confirming alignment on requirements, timelines, and decisions, and escalating incomplete, delayed, or competing requests before they affect program milestones
* **Requirements, SOW & SLA Readiness:** Translate operating requirements into sourcing-ready scope — including volumes, sites, timing, constraints, and acceptance criteria — and track development of statements of work and service-level agreements to identify gaps before a bid is issued or a contract is executed
* **Capital Expenditure & Multi-Project Execution:** Manage milestone tracking for high-visibility and capex logistics programs (factory and line installations, equipment and tooling moves, project deployments, and build-outs where logistics is on the critical path), running several projects in parallel across freight, warehousing, parcel, brokerage, project cargo, and specialized moves while maintaining an integrated schedule and adjusting plans when programs compete for the same capacity
* **Procurement Interface & Service Transition:** Partner with logistics supply chain managers on sourcing timelines, data requests, and decision gates to ensure each event is supported by a complete request and confirmed stakeholder participation; following award, verify that SOWs are executed, service levels are understood, site briefings are complete, and the service is operational before treating the program as closed
* **Cross-Functional Partnership:** Work with operations teams, construction and program teams, Material Planning, Service Parts, Finance, Legal, Trade & Customs, and Logistics Operations; represent program status in launch, peak-readiness, and capital reviews; and resolve issues that stand between a stakeholder request and an executed service agreement
* **Team Contribution:** Coach analysts and cross-functional partners on how to define a logistics request, the content required in a statement of work, and how to interpret a program timeline; serve as the day-to-day program coordinator and first escalation point when a program is off schedule

 **What You'll Bring**

* **Education & Experience:** Bachelor's Degree in Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience with 5–8 years coordinating logistics, supply chain, or procurement programs between operations stakeholders and procurement — preferably within a complex manufacturing environment — including demonstrated ability to manage several concurrent programs with at least one large-scale or capital program, or equivalent experience
* **Leadership & Influence:** Ability to influence operations leaders and Global Supply Managers without direct authority, maintain schedule discipline when inputs are delayed, and present status and recommendations to Director-level stakeholders
* **Technical Skills:** Ability to convert an operations request into a defined requirement covering sites, volumes, timing, constraints, and service levels; working knowledge of logistics service procurement including RFIs/RFPs, statements of work, SLAs, and award transition; ability to maintain a milestone plan, RACI, and risk log across multiple programs including capital projects; experience across plant logistics and project or site logistics (expertise in every transportation mode is not required); advanced Excel with Power BI or equivalent analytics tool experience a plus
* **Soft Skills & Process Knowledge:** Strong written communication, facilitation, and follow-through with the ability to align requesting stakeholders and supply managers while respecting the accountability of each team; solid command of purchasing processes including SOPs, RFIs/RFPs, statements of work, SLAs, purchase orders, and contract governance
* **Other Requirements:** Fluent in English; willingness to travel ~20–30% to Tesla sites and supplier reviews; based in Fremont, CA; passion for Tesla's mission

#### **Benefits**

Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:

* Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
* Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
* Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
* Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
* Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* 401

* Create and maintain team documentation and training materials to support consistent processes and knowledge sharing.
* Create ad hoc provider rosters and perform data analysis as requested by partner teams to support operational needs, escalations, and audits.

* Assist with provider data discrepancies escalated by practices and partner teams by researching the issue, coordinating corrections, and confirming updates are reflected in downstream systems and deliverables.

**Company Description**

**Appointment Type:** This is a Temporary Provisional (TPV) position excluded by the Charter from the competitive Civil Service examination process. It is considered "at will" and shall serve at the discretion of the Department Head. This position will be subject to the Permanent Civil Service examination process at a later date. Successful participation in the Permanent Civil Service examination and selection through an open competitive process is needed in order to be considered for the permanent appointment.

Compensation Range: $129,636 - $157,612 annually

Recruitment ID: RTF0168079-01156693

**Who We Are**

Through the provision of coordinated, compassionate, and high‐quality services, the Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH) strives to make homelessness in San Francisco rare, brief, and one time. The Department provides assistance and support to homeless and at‐risk youth, adults, and families to prevent imminent episodes of homelessness and end homelessness for people in San Francisco. Services including outreach, homelessness prevention, emergency shelter, drop‐in centers, transitional housing, supportive housing, short‐term rental subsidies, and support services to help people exit homelessness. For more information about the department, please visit our website at https://hsh.sfgov.org.

**What We Do**

San Francisco is a pioneer in homeless services and a leader in providing supportive housing as a permanent exit from homelessness. The Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH), founded in 2016, is a national leader in the movement to end homelessness by developing a coordinated, equity-driven, client-focused system of compassionate services while piloting innovative models, and implementing best practice solutions with measurable results.

HSH’s Homelessness Response System (HRS) funds, oversees and implements a system of care that shelters, houses, and serves approximately 15,000 people daily. Major programs include: street outreach and service connection through the Homeless Outreach Team (SFHOT); 3,600+ bed shelter system for transitional age youth, adults and families including shelters for members of the LGBTQ community; Rapid Rehousing rental subsidies for families, adults, older adults, and transitional aged youth; the Problem Solving and flexible financial assistance programs; and robust supportive housing programs with over 14,500 units which provide housing and services to formerly homeless transitional age youth, individuals, and families.

The Rapid Rehousing Program Manager supports the planning, implementation, oversight, and continuous improvement of Rapid Rehousing programs funded by HSH. Rapid Rehousing provides time-limited rental assistance and supportive services to help people experiencing homelessness obtain housing in the private rental market and transition toward long-term housing stability, including nonprofit provider agreements, program budgets, utilization, housing placements, participant outcomes, and program performance.

HSH has a longstanding portfolio of Rapid Rehousing programs, and the City continues to invest in and expand these programs as part of its Breaking the Cycle strategy. The Program Manager will play a central role in implementing this investment and the next phase of HSH's RRH portfolio, including implementation of newly procured programs and provider agreements, provider and program transitions, and efforts to strengthen and standardize program operations. The position will help ensure that new and existing investments translate into timely referrals and housing placements, strong program utilization, effective provider performance, and successful participant outcomes.

The Program Manager works across HSH and with nonprofit providers, Coordinated Entry, housing partners, other City departments, and governmental and community partners to translate HSH's housing strategies into effective program operations. The position uses program, fiscal, and performance data to identify challenges, develop solutions, and recommend changes to program design, policy, funding, and operations. The Rapid Rehousing Program Manager reports to the Scattered Site Housing Programs Supervisor and is part of HSH's Housing Division.

* Implements new and reprocured RRH programs, provider transitions, and other program changes.

* Monitors program budgets and expenditures and supports budget development, projections, revisions, and modifications.
* Monitors referrals, enrollment, utilization, housing placements, exits, and housing retention outcomes.
* Works with providers to identify and address program performance concerns and improve outcomes.
* Ensures providers deliver housing stabilization and retention services to support participants following housing placement and through successful program exit.
* Analyzes program, fiscal, and ONE System/HMIS data to identify trends, barriers, and opportunities for program improvement.

new_jobs.title: D365 Project Manager, Managed Services
new_jobs.description:
**Location** Virtual, home based office with travel

**Description**

The MCA Connect Project Manager in this role carries a blended portfolio. You will manage day to day support for live Dynamics 365 clients under Managed Services (MgS), manage the discrete enhancement and new functionality work those same clients buy, and direct one or more full life-cycle Dynamics 365 implementations from diagnosis through go-live and transition into support.

  

These three types of work are genuinely different disciplines.

* MgS live support is a queue to be managed against service commitments.
* New functionality and enhancement work is a series of small, fixed-scope projects that must be estimated, scheduled and billed without disturbing the support commitment.
* A full life-cycle implementation is a large, multi-phase program with its own team, budget and executive visibility.

  

The person in this role must be able to manage all three at once, switch cleanly between them, and protect each from the others.

  

You will be supported by a strong delivery team of solution architects, functional and technical consultants, and developers, but you will need a strong background in project management and business process optimization, and either a solid working knowledge of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 platform or the capacity to build one quickly. Our projects are strategic investments for our clients. Their successful execution and their ongoing support both require a project manager who is driven, proactive, creative, assertive and relationship oriented.

  

While your primary function is project management, from time to time you may also be asked to assist with other functions including sales and marketing, implementation-related tasks, and general administration.

### **Responsibilities**

The responsibilities below are grouped into the disciplines common to every engagement, then the three work streams in turn, then the financial, communication and practice duties that run across all of them. Each group opens with what the work is and why it matters, followed by the specific tasks the role owns.

**Core project management, all work streams**
---------------------------------------------

A set of project management disciplines applies to every engagement you carry, whatever its size or commercial shape.

* Manage multiple concurrent client engagements, and own deliverables, scope and expectations on each of them.
* Provide leadership to all functional and business areas affected by the work.
* Develop and maintain project plans, cost estimates, resource plans, communication plans, risk mitigation plans and issue resolution plans.
* Drive project decisions and make recommendations to management about schedules, prioritization and resource allocation.
* Work with MCA Connect resource management to secure resources, and resolve the challenges between support needs, enhancement commitments and other milestones.
* Employ project management leading practices as provided by PMI and MCA Connect delivery standards.
* Drive client satisfaction across the portfolio and own the health relationship of every account you carry.

**MgS live support clients**
----------------------------

For an assigned portfolio of live Dynamics 365 clients, the work is a managed queue rather than a plan: tickets arrive on their own schedule to a support queue, and your job is to see that they are triaged correctly, worked by the right consultant, resolved inside the contracted commitment, and visible to the client throughout. Alongside the queue you monitor consumption against contract in period and raise the conversation about overage or change before the period closes rather than after.

* Own the service relationship for each assigned live client and act as their main point of accountability.
* Manage the client’s service desk tickets: triage, prioritization, assignment, aging, escalation and closure.
* Balance case load across the available consultant pool and keep the queue from concentrating on one person.
* Run regular service reviews covering ticket volumes and trends, consumption against the retainer or hours block, open risks and the forward plan.
* Manage environment optimization and management activities, including release and update readiness for Microsoft's service update cadence, environment refreshes and performance reviews.
* Monitor consumption against contract in period and flag over-consumption and under-consumption early.
* Drive the conversation about overage, carry-over or contract change before the period closes.
* Convert recurring incidents and chronic pain points into problem records, root cause work or scoped enhancement proposals.
* Maintain accurate case records, time capture and status in Symphony so reporting, invoicing and utilization figures reconcile without manual correction.
* Receive projects transitioning in from the implementation team and confirm documentation, environments, known issues and open items all transferred.

**New functionality and enhancement delivery**
----------------------------------------------

Live clients regularly buy work that is not support. Further work could be a customization, implement a new D365 module, an integration change, a business process review, or a training package. Each of these is a small project in its own right. The recurring tension in this stream is resource: enhancement work and the support queue draw on the same consultants, and you are expected to schedule around that rather than let one quietly starve the other.

* Qualify incoming requests, distinguish enhancements from support incidents, and route each to the right resources.
* Coordinate estimation with solution architects and consultants, and produce the scope, effort, schedule and price the client will approve.
* Secure written client approval of scope, cost and schedule before work begins.
* Schedule enhancement work packages against the same resource pool that carries the support

DRT Strategies delivers expert management consulting and information technology (IT) solutions to large federal agencies, state and local government and commercial clients in health care, technology, and financial services industries.

**Project Description:**  
The position is in the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the Office of the Commissioner (OC), Office of the Chief Scientist (OCS), Office of Regulatory and Emerging Science (ORES). * Three years should be closely involved with practical aircraft carrier/surface ship (as applicable) maintenance, design, operation, and other problems of main propulsion, auxiliary,electrical, and damage control equipment associated with shipboard level maintenance.

Serco North America is seeking a **Program & Data Analyst** to provide programmatic, analytical, and operational support to **Team Submarine** for a major U.S. Navy modernization and sustainment program at the Washington Navy Yard in Washington, D.C.

**Must be able to obtain/maintain/transfer a U.S. Department of War (DoW) Secret security clearance.**

In this role, you will serve as a key contributor supporting program execution, stakeholder coordination, data analysis, and reporting across U.S. Navy and Department of Defense organizations. You will transform complex data into meaningful insights by collecting, validating, analyzing, and presenting information that enables informed, data-driven decision-making and supports successful program outcomes.

The successful candidate will provide senior leadership with objective, data-informed information and recommendations supporting decisions related to program execution, organizational effectiveness, and management operations. You will compile, maintain, verify, and interpret data using established organizational plans, policies, and independent judgment; perform in-depth analyses to identify trends, anomalies, risks, and potential technical or management issues; and develop reports, recommendations, and support documentation for senior-level review.

This is not a telework/hybrid position.***

In this role, you will:

* Compile, maintain, verify, interpret, and analyze program and operational data to support program execution and senior-level decision-making.
* Analyze large and complex data sets and develop data analytics and visualization tools to identify trends, anomalies, risks, and actionable insights.

Amentum is seeking a **Cybersecurity Analyst** to join our team and support our **McLean, VA** customer. We are looking for team members who are passionate about making a difference by working on critical efforts we manage as a premier government contractor.

Here at Amentum, we are purpose-driven with a fierce commitment to deliver on our promises. We create trailblazing solutions, have unwavering integrity, and embrace inclusion and collaboration. Our team is excited to help customers solve todays and tomorrow’s problems, giving confidence and reassurance that together we’ll accomplish mission success.

**Purpose / Scope:**

The Cybersecurity Analyst will perform assessment and authorization (A&A) efforts under the NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF) on behalf of a federal civilian agency as a contractor. The role will conduct cybersecurity analysis in preparation for A&A reviewing and validation of all associated cybersecurity documentation and technical controls.

The role will work within a team that conducts A&A activities. This individual will develop System Security Plans (SSP), Contingency Plans, Business Impact Analyses (BIA), Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), Security Assessment Report (SARs), Security Assessment Plan (SAPs), and other RMF documentation.

This position covers all cybersecurity aspects including, but not limited to, identifying risks, validating the mitigation of plans of action, analyzing system designs, and assisting with A&A issues that may prevent a system from receiving authorization. It supports the implementation of RMF by developing documentation and updating policies, procedures, and processes as assigned.

Contribute to the security planning, assessment, risk analysis, risk management, certification and awareness activities for system and networking operations. * One or more of the following certifications preferred (Security+, CAP, CISSP, CISM, GSEC, GCIH, or GSLC)

* Familiar with dealing with defense-in-depth, and other information security and assurance principles and associated supporting technologies

* Must demonstrate proficiency in the following areas: multi-tasking, critical thinking; and the ability to work quickly, efficiently and accurately in a dynamic and fluid environment
* Must have a Top-Secret Clearance with polygraph
* Must be able to read, speak, write, and understand the English language

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* BA/BS Degree
* Excellent oral and written communication skills
* Ability to interact and relay security technical requirements at all levels of leadership and work force
* Ability to work both independently and as a member of a team

Typical office environment with no unusual hazards, occasional lifting to 20 pounds, constant sitting while using the computer terminal, constant use of sight abilities while reviewing documents, constant use of speech/hearing abilities for communication, constant mental alertness, must possess planning/organizing skills, and must be able to work under deadlines.

This role serves as the central point of contact for daily office operations, records management, travel logistics, and personnel tracking. Active Secret Clearance Required.

* **Document & Records Control:** Set up and maintain digital and hard-copy files according to DCSA policy. Properly handle, mark, and destroy classified and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI).
* **Correspondence:** Draft, format, and proofread high-quality official letters, memos, reports, and executive presentations.
* **Travel & Fleet Management:** Assist staff with Defense Travel System (DTS) travel orders and vouchers. Coordinate Government Owned Vehicle (GOV) logs, dispatch, maintenance, and data entry.
* **Personnel & HR Logistics:** Support civilian employee onboarding/offboarding, track recruitment event milestones, sort resumes, and maintain training records.

Muon Space seeks a Senior Program Manager to lead delivery of next-generation satellites for national security missions, including missile warning and tracking. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role at the intersection of payload engineering and rapid-cycle space vehicle development.

The Senior PM is the accountable owner for delivering the program on cost, schedule, and technical performance. You will manage a multi-disciplinary internal team, subcontractors, and a critical-path vendor base for EO/IR payloads, algorithm development, avionics, and space vehicle builds. The role spans the full program lifecycle: design reviews, hardware build, integration and environmental test, launch, and on-orbit operations.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* **Program Execution**
  + Own the integrated master schedule, cost baseline, and risk register
  + Drive the program through preliminary and critical design reviews, payload and spacecraft integration, environmental test, launch, and on-orbit demonstration, meeting customer milestones and contract deliverables
  + Manage scope, cost, and period of performance against contract milestones and payment events

Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. new_jobs.title: Logistics Procurement Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
**What to Expect**

Tesla is focused on building a world of abundance and we are seeking a Logistics Procurement Program Manager to manage execution of logistics procurement programs. You will coordinate between the operations stakeholders requesting logistics services and logistics supply chain managers responsible for sourcing those services. You will ensure that requirements, statements of work, and service-level agreements are defined, aligned, and progressing, and that major programs, including capital expenditure programs, advance from request through start of service on an agreed timeline. You will manage multiple logistics projects concurrently, across the modes each program requires. Category strategy and commercial negotiation remain with the supply managers. This is a high-ownership role for someone who can keep a portfolio of programs on schedule and present status, risks, and decisions to a broad group of stakeholders.

  
**What You'll Do**

* **Program Portfolio Ownership & Governance:** Own a cross-category portfolio of logistics programs by establishing scope, timelines, accountable owners, and success criteria for each; maintain a program operating cadence including milestone reviews, a risk log, and status reporting suitable for leadership; and ensure a repeatable coordination process that does not depend on a single individual
* **Stakeholder Coordination & Escalation:** Serve as the coordination point between operations stakeholders requesting logistics services and supply chain managers procuring them, confirming alignment on requirements, timelines, and decisions, and escalating incomplete, delayed, or competing requests before they affect program milestones
* **Requirements, SOW & SLA Readiness:** Translate operating requirements into sourcing-ready scope — including volumes, sites, timing, constraints, and acceptance criteria — and track development of statements of work and service-level agreements to identify gaps before a bid is issued or a contract is executed
* **Capital Expenditure & Multi-Project Execution:** Manage milestone tracking for high-visibility and capex logistics programs (factory and line installations, equipment and tooling moves, project deployments, and build-outs where logistics is on the critical path), running several projects in parallel across freight, warehousing, parcel, brokerage, project cargo, and specialized moves while maintaining an integrated schedule and adjusting plans when programs compete for the same capacity
* **Procurement Interface & Service Transition:** Partner with logistics supply chain managers on sourcing timelines, data requests, and decision gates to ensure each event is supported by a complete request and confirmed stakeholder participation; following award, verify that SOWs are executed, service levels are understood, site briefings are complete, and the service is operational before treating the program as closed
* **Cross-Functional Partnership:** Work with operations teams, construction and program teams, Material Planning, Service Parts, Finance, Legal, Trade & Customs, and Logistics Operations; represent program status in launch, peak-readiness, and capital reviews; and resolve issues that stand between a stakeholder request and an executed service agreement
* **Team Contribution:** Coach analysts and cross-functional partners on how to define a logistics request, the content required in a statement of work, and how to interpret a program timeline; serve as the day-to-day program coordinator and first escalation point when a program is off schedule

 **What You'll Bring**

* **Education & Experience:** Bachelor's Degree in Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience with 5–8 years coordinating logistics, supply chain, or procurement programs between operations stakeholders and procurement — preferably within a complex manufacturing environment — including demonstrated ability to manage several concurrent programs with at least one large-scale or capital program, or equivalent experience
* **Leadership & Influence:** Ability to influence operations leaders and Global Supply Managers without direct authority, maintain schedule discipline when inputs are delayed, and present status and recommendations to Director-level stakeholders
* **Technical Skills:** Ability to convert an operations request into a defined requirement covering sites, volumes, timing, constraints, and service levels; working knowledge of logistics service procurement including RFIs/RFPs, statements of work, SLAs, and award transition; ability to maintain a milestone plan, RACI, and risk log across multiple programs including capital projects; experience across plant logistics and project or site logistics (expertise in every transportation mode is not required); advanced Excel with Power BI or equivalent analytics tool experience a plus
* **Soft Skills & Process Knowledge:** Strong written communication, facilitation, and follow-through with the ability to align requesting stakeholders and supply managers while respecting the accountability of each team; solid command of purchasing processes including SOPs, RFIs/RFPs, statements of work, SLAs, purchase orders, and contract governance
* **Other Requirements:** Fluent in English; willingness to travel ~20–30% to Tesla sites and supplier reviews; based in Fremont, CA; passion for Tesla's mission

#### **Benefits**

Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:

* Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
* Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
* Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
* Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
* Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* 401
